title: Trigonometric Functions and Periodic Models
description: A point starts at (1,0) and rotates counterclockwise one revolution in 8 seconds. Sketch its vertical coordinate against time and label zeros, extrema, and period.
outcomes: Construct y=sin t from the vertical coordinate of a rotating unit-circle point.
Construct y=cos t from the horizontal coordinate of circular motion and compare it with sine.
Interpret A and D in y=A sin x+D or y=A cos x+D.
Relate inside scale B to period, ordinary frequency, and angular frequency.
Interpret B(x-C) as a horizontal timing shift and recover C from graph or context.
Build and analyze y=A sin(B(x-C))+D and equivalent cosine forms.
Derive tangent and cotangent graphs from quotient definitions, zeros, asymptotes, and period pi.
Construct secant and cosecant graphs as reciprocals of cosine and sine.
Compare domains, ranges, parity, periods, zeros, and asymptotes of all six trig functions.
Define inverse sine, cosine, and tangent using one-to-one branches and principal-value ranges.
Solve sin x=k, cos x=k, and tan x=k using exact values, inverse functions, periodicity, and interval restrictions.
Fit and critique sinusoidal models using amplitude, midline, period, phase, residuals, and domain.
sources: AP Precalculus framework, Trigonometric and Polar Functions
